self_critique:
The run found a small improvement, but converged prematurely after only three follow-ups.

What was suboptimal

- Node_001 changed several factors simultaneously: MLP dropout, embedding L2, AdamW decay, and LR decay. This obscures which change produced the +0.0014 gain and makes subsequent tuning inefficient.
- Node_003 had the highest displayed score (0.6034) yet was rejected while best_primary remained 0.603157. This may be correct under a significance or complexity gate, but the journal does not record the rejection margin, uncertainty, or criterion. That makes the decision unauditable.
- Stopping after two rejected children is too aggressive, especially when one nominally exceeded the incumbent. The search did not exhaust obvious local ablations or parameter sweeps.
- The BPR experiment bundled a new objective with complete-user batching and a relatively large fixed mixing weight. Its failure does not establish that pairwise supervision is unhelpful.
- Claimed gains of +0.002 to +0.005 were not well calibrated to the observed effect sizes. There was no explicit multi-seed or paired uncertainty estimate for each candidate; the baseline sigma alone is insufficient.
- Recency was tested at one half-life and one floor. A single setting cannot adequately evaluate the hypothesis.

Scaffold changes

- Require one-factor ablations after a bundled winner. Independently test dropout, embedding regularization, dense weight decay, and LR decay.
- Record full-precision score, delta, acceptance threshold, variance/confidence interval, and exact rejection reason for every node.
- Use cheap single-seed screening followed by paired multi-seed confirmation for candidates near or above the incumbent.
- Do not declare convergence merely after two rejections. Require exhaustion of a small local neighborhood or a defined budget/patience rule.
- Separate objective changes from batching changes. For pairwise losses, sweep small weights such as 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 before 0.3.
- Preserve secondary metrics and segment-level results so small aggregate changes can be diagnosed.

What the next run should try first

First, rerun node_003 against node_001 over multiple matched seeds. Its nominal score is the strongest result in the journal, so resolving whether the gain is real has highest value. If confirmed, sweep recency half-lives around 3, 7, 14, and 28 days and tune or remove the stale-row floor.

In parallel, ablate node_001’s four regularizers one at a time. This should identify the actual source of improvement and provide a cleaner incumbent before revisiting a lower-weight BCE+BPR hybrid.
